challenges.name: value-reference-numbers-quiz
challenges.title: Predict it: copies, integer division and rounding
challenges.description: Follow a struct and a class through an assignment, then decide which number snippets behave the way their authors expected.

questions.explanation: Seat is a struct, a value type: var b = a copies every field, so b is a separate Seat and b.Row = 2 leaves a.Row at 1. Desk is a class, a reference type: var d = c copies only the reference, so c and d are two names for one Desk object, and d.Row = 2 is visible through c. The output is "1 2". "1 1" is what you would get if Desk were a struct too, "2 2" if Seat were a class. "2 1" cannot happen with any combination.

questions.question: Which of these statements are true? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: attended / sessions is int / int, so 9 / 12 is 0 and 0 * 100 is 0: write 100.0 * attended / sessions. Math.Round(2.5m) uses MidpointRounding.ToEven by default and returns 2 (the nearest even number); pass MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero to get 3. var fee = 1_800_000 makes fee an int, and fee * 1.1 is a double, so the assignment is the compile error CS0266 "Cannot implicitly convert type 'double' to 'int'". string, arrays and classes are reference types; int, decimal, bool and structs are value types. decimal stores 0.1, 0.2 and 0.3 exactly, so 0.1m + 0.2m == 0.3m is true (with double it is false: 0.30000000000000004). int[] b = a copies the reference to the one array, so b[0] = 9 also changes a[0].

options.text: int sessions = 12, attended = 9; Console.WriteLine(attended / sessions * 100); prints 0
var fee = 1_800_000; fee = fee * 1.1; compiles, and fee becomes 1980000
string, arrays and classes are reference types; int, decimal, bool and structs are value types
int[] a = [1, 2]; int[] b = a; b[0] = 9; leaves a[0] equal to 1

challenges.name: monthly-tuition-invoices
challenges.title: Write the monthly tuition invoices
challenges.description: Sen Academy bills every student the class's monthly fee minus their discount (a scholarship, a sibling discount), in whole VND. Write AmountDue, Total and Average: compute each amount with decimal and round half a đồng up the way the accountant does, add up a whole school without overflowing, and average the amounts. The test runner reads one student per line (id, monthly fee, discount percent) and prints each amount, the total and the average.
